rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The Haber process fixes atmospheric nitrogen by the compromise of all compromises: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ at 200–300 atm, 450–500 °C over promoted iron — hot enough to run, cool enough to yield, pressurised for three independent reasons (equilibrium's fewer moles, collision-dense rate, ammonia's raised dew point), and looped so that a 15% per-pass conversion becomes ~97% overall.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Haber Process: Feeding the World from Air Ammonia is the gateway to every nitrogenous fertiliser. The Haber process combines **N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ + heat (ΔH ≈ −92 kJ/mol)** under high pressure, moderate temperature and an iron catalyst — the single most consequential equilibrium compromise in industry, fixing the nitrogen that feeds roughly half the world's population.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Reaction:** N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = −92 kJ/mol; 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas. - **Conditions:** pressure **200–300 atm**; temperature **450–500 °C**; catalyst **finely divided iron** promoted with K₂O/Al₂O₃ (or Mo) — the promoters increase surface activity and resist sintering.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The 450-500 C operating point is neither yield-optimal nor rate-optimal - it is the profit optimum, and the recycle loop pays for the shortfall.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: N2 + 3H2 <-> 2NH3, dH = -92 kJ/mol, 4 mol -> 2 mol. Conditions: 200-300 atm, 450-500 C, finely divided Fe with K2O/Al2O3 promoters. Feeds: N2 from liquid air; H2 by steam reforming (CH4 + H2O -> CO + 3H2) + shift (CO + H2O -> CO2 + H2). Flow: compress -> converter -> condenser (-33 C bp) -> recycle.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Haber process fixes the nitrogen feeding roughly half the world's population - the most consequential equilibrium compromise in industry.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — The Compromise That Runs the World - Thermodynamics and kinetics pull opposite ways: **low T maximises yield, high T maximises rate.** The 450–500 °C operating point is neither the yield optimum nor the rate optimum — it is the *profit* optimum: enough rate per pass to make the plant pay, with the yield shortfall recovered by recycling.…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Why High Pressure Is a Three-Layer Answer - **Equilibrium layer:** 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas; Le Chatelier ⟹ pressure favours the ammonia side, raising the per-pass mole fraction. - **Rate layer:** high pressure concentrates the molecules — more collisions per second — so the iron catalyst works on a denser gas, accelerating the slow N₂ activation.…  ·  ### Deep dive — Haber: an equilibrium argument turned into 150 million tonnes N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH = −92 kJ, Δn = −2. Le Chatelier says high pressure and low temperature favour ammonia — but low temperature is uselessly slow. The industrial compromise: **200–300 atm, 450–500 °C, Fe catalyst (with Mo or K₂O/Al₂O₅ promoters)**, and continuous removal of NH₃ by liquefaction.…
